summary.text: Chosen king of Thebes when Autesion departed for the Dorians — in Pausanias' reckoning, a son of Opheltes son of Peneleos, and one of the last sole rulers before the Thebans divided the government among several magistrates.

His son Ptolemy (`ptolemy-theban`) fathered Xanthus (`xanthus-theban`), who fell in a duel with Andropompus (`andropompus-theban`); after Xanthus' death the Thebans thought it better not to let everything depend on one man.
Not to be confused with Damasichthon son of Amphion and Niobe, slain by Apollo's arrows, or with Damasichthon son of Codrus, the Ionian king at Colophon.

story.text: Pausanias closes the Theban monarchy with a short roll of Peneleid kings. On Autesion's departure, Damasichthon was chosen — son of Opheltes, son of Peneleos the Boeotian captain who had led Thebes to Troy in young Tisamenus' stead and fallen to Eurypylus son of Telephus.

This Damasichthon had a son Ptolemy, who was the father of Xanthus. When Xanthus fought a duel with Andropompus and was killed by craft rather than in fair fight, the Thebans changed their constitution: hereafter they thought it better to entrust the government to several people, rather than to let everything depend on one man — the end, in Pausanias' telling, of single kingship at seven-gated Thebes.
